one_liner: Research SIMD (AVX-512/IFMA) kernels for bignum add/sub and base-case multiply, patched into GMP and OpenSSL.
what_it_does: DigitsOnTurbo (DoT) is a 2026 arXiv preprint (Das, Bichhawat, Patel; IIT Gandhinagar and Edinburgh) with about 1,000 lines of C intrinsics that replace GMP's mpn_add_n, mpn_sub_n and 256-bit base-case multiplication, plus the matching OpenSSL bignum primitives. It is not a library you call directly: the authors add it to GMP (DoTMP) and OpenSSL (DoTSSL) with about 40 lines of changes, so existing mpz/BN code picks it up unchanged.
how_it_is_fast: Add/sub runs in four phases: lane-parallel limb add, carry detection with SIMD compares, a single parallel carry-propagation step, and a deferred scalar slow path for cascading carries. A cascade requires limbs equal to 2^64-1, so on random inputs it practically never fires. Multiplication uses a 'vertical and crosswise' scheme that exposes all m^2 partial products as independent AVX-512 IFMA multiplies (52-bit radix, with conversion from 64-bit limbs) before reducing columns, which removes read-after-write chains on a shared accumulator. Karatsuba/Toom recursion in GMP bottoms out in this base case.
when_to_use: Research or prototyping on AVX-512 (Sapphire/Emerald Rapids class) Xeons where GMP mpn add/sub dominates the profile
Mid-size operands (about 6,144-32,768 bits), where the paper reports its largest gains
Reproducing or extending SIMD bignum work; the four-phase carry design is a clear reference
Estimating headroom before investing in your own SIMD mpn kernels
when_not_to_use: Production work: there is no public repository or license, and the code sits at an anonymous review URL
CPUs without AVX-512: the paper reports SSE addition at 0.7x (slower than scalar) and AVX2 at only 1.2x
Huge-operand multiplication dominated by FFT: DoT replaces only the base case, so whole-program gains shrink (GMPbench +7.8% overall)
Crypto code that needs constant time: the data-dependent cascading-carry slow path is not analysed for timing leaks
Adversarial inputs built to trigger cascading carries, where the paper's advantage drops to 0.7-2.0x versus prior SIMD methods

integration.dependencies: GMP 6.3.0 or OpenSSL 3.5.2 source tree to patch
integration.min_toolchain: evaluated with clang 14, -O2 -march=native; others not documented
integration.platforms: x86-64; AVX-512 (plus IFMA for multiply) needed for the reported gains
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it patches GMP/OpenSSL internals (about 40 lines) so the public API stays the same, but you must rebuild those libraries from patched source

gotchas: The code was not verifiable: anonymous.4open.science blocks fetchers, and no license is stated
The headline 3.81x/3.73x geomeans are for the add/sub primitives alone; end-to-end gains are much smaller (pi +19.3%, divide +8.4%, RSA/FFDH/DSA throughput +3-5%)
The multiply needs a 64-to-52-bit radix conversion for the 4x4 routine to stay compatible with GMP/OpenSSL limbs, which adds overhead
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over ctbignum or mp++ only if you want faster stock GMP/OpenSSL arithmetic at thousands of bits on AVX-512 without changing your code, and you can live with unpublished code. FLINT is the shippable choice for big-number workloads, and the truncated-batch AVX-512 Montgomery code fits better when you batch modular exponentiations.
verified_claims_summary: Against stock GMP 6.3.0, DoT-patched GMP gives geomean 3.81x add, 3.73x sub and 1.41x multiply over 512-32,768-bit operands, up to 48.7% on large multiplies and +19.3% on pi. Against OpenSSL 3.5.2 it gives 2.95x add and 4.08x sub. All results are from clang 14 -O2 -march=native on Xeon Gold 6548Y+ (Emerald Rapids) and Xeon Max 9462 (Sapphire Rapids), measured by the authors.
status_note: Preprint with no stated venue and code only at an anonymous review link with no license, so treat it as a reference design, not a dependency; maintenance status unknown.
